title: Choose the discourse marker
instructions: Write the missing word(s) in each mini-dialogue.

items.q: The flat is expensive. ______ you, it's the only one near the station.
He can be quite rude. To be ______, he did apologise afterwards.
So, going ______ to what I was saying about the budget...
As I ______, the deadline is fixed - we can't move it.
A: 'The traffic this morning was awful.'  B: 'Tell me ______ it!'
A: 'I'd rather not talk about it.'  B: 'Fair ______.'
A: 'I'm leaving the company.'  B: 'Really? How ______?'
It's a great city to live in. Then ______, the winters are terrible.
Anyway, that's ______ the point. What I wanted to ask was...
I know ______ you mean - I had exactly the same problem.

title: Make it sound C1
instructions: Rewrite each B2-style sentence so that it sounds more nuanced, diplomatic or natural. Compare with the models.

a: I'm not sure that's quite right.
I'm not entirely convinced that's the case.
I see it a bit differently, actually.
I like where you're going with this, but I'm not sure it'd work in practice.
I have a few reservations about that.
I can see a couple of potential issues with that.
Exactly - that's what I was thinking.
I wouldn't be surprised if it rained.
I've got a feeling it's going to rain.

items.q: I don't know the word... eh... the thing for opening wine.
a: What do you call it... the thing you use to get the cork out of a wine bottle?
You know, the gadget with a spiral bit that you twist into the cork.

items.q: You are late again. This is a problem.
a: I've noticed you've been running late quite a lot recently - is everything OK?
I just wanted to mention timekeeping - it's started to affect the team. Is there anything getting in the way?
The report needs another proofread - I've flagged quite a few errors.
I think the report could do with another pass before it goes out.
Could we find some time to talk about my salary?
I'd like to discuss the possibility of a raise (BrE: pay rise), based on what I've delivered this year.
Could you send me the report when you get a chance?
Would you mind sending over the report?
I'm afraid that's not something we can do at the moment.
Unfortunately, that won't be possible - but what we could do is...
I'm running a bit behind on that - I'll have it to you by tomorrow morning.
That's taken longer than expected; can I get it to you by Thursday?
I don't think I explained that very clearly - let me clarify.
Sorry, I think my email may have been a bit confusing.

title: Choose the most natural professional response
instructions: Choose the response a skilled C1 speaker would most likely use. Careful: some wrong options are typical Spanish-speaker calques.

items.q: A colleague proposes an unrealistic deadline.
options: With the greatest respect, that's not realistic.
I'm afraid that deadline is simply impossible.
That might be a bit tight - could we walk through the timeline together?
a: That might be a bit tight - could we walk through the timeline together?
c) That might be a bit tight - could we walk through the timeline together?

items.q: Your manager asks your opinion on a plan you don't like.
options: Honestly? I don't think it's a good plan.
I can see the logic behind it, but I do have a couple of concerns.
It's very interesting.
a: I can see the logic behind it, but I do have a couple of concerns.
b) I can see the logic behind it, but I do have a couple of concerns.

items.q: You didn't understand what someone said in a meeting.
options: Can you repeat, please?
Sorry, I didn't quite catch that - could you say it again?
Sorry, what?
a: Sorry, I didn't quite catch that - could you say it again?
b) Sorry, I didn't quite catch that - could you say it again?

items.q: You need more time to answer a difficult question.
options: Good question - give me a second to think about that.
Wait, wait...
I don't know, sorry.
a: Good question - give me a second to think about that.
a) Good question - give me a second to think about that.

options: Sorry, but I must interrupt you.
Excuse me, I want to say something.
Sorry to jump in - could I just add something here?
a: Sorry to jump in - could I just add something here?
c) Sorry to jump in - could I just add something here?

items.q: Someone makes a good point that changes your mind.
options: Maybe. We'll see.
Actually, that's a fair point - I hadn't looked at it that way.
OK, you are right and I was wrong.
a: Actually, that's a fair point - I hadn't looked at it that way.
b) Actually, that's a fair point - I hadn't looked at it that way.

items.q: You need a file from a colleague by Friday (email).
options: Send me the file on Friday, please.
Would you be able to send it over by Friday?
I need the file for Friday.
a: Would you be able to send it over by Friday?
b) Would you be able to send it over by Friday?

items.q: You're asked to take on extra work you don't have time for.
options: I'd love to help, but I don't have the bandwidth this week - could it wait until Monday?
Impossible, I have too much work.
No, I can't. I'm very busy.
a: I'd love to help, but I don't have the bandwidth this week - could it wait until Monday?
a) I'd love to help, but I don't have the bandwidth this week - could it wait until Monday?

items.q: On a video call, the other person's audio drops out.
options: I don't hear you.
Sorry, you cut out for a second - could you repeat the last bit?
Your connection is bad.
a: Sorry, you cut out for a second - could you repeat the last bit?
b) Sorry, you cut out for a second - could you repeat the last bit?

title: -ed endings
instructions: How is the -ed ending pronounced? Write t, d or id. Say each word aloud before answering.

title: -s endings
instructions: How is the -s ending pronounced? Write s, z or iz. Say it aloud first.

title: Word stress
instructions: Which syllable is stressed? Write the number (1 = first syllable). Check tricky ones in the Cambridge Dictionary and listen.

title: Which word carries the main stress?
instructions: Read the context, then write the ONE word that gets the main (nuclear) stress in B's reply.

items.q: A: Did you buy the red one?  B: 'No, I bought the blue one.'
A: Who sent the email?  B: 'Maria sent it.'
A: You didn't send it, did you?  B: 'I did send it.'
A: Is the meeting on Monday?  B: 'No, it's on Tuesday.'
A: I love London.  B: 'I hate London.'
A: Where do you work?  B: 'I work in a bank.'
A: Coffee?  B: 'I'd prefer tea, actually.'
A: I thought you lived in Madrid.  B: 'I used to live in Madrid.'
A: Is it your car?  B: 'No, it's my sister's car.'
A glass building for growing plants: a GREENhouse or a green HOUSE? Write the stressed word.
